reason: The text contains a clear passage where the Israelites blame Moses (their leader) for putting them in danger. After seeing the Egyptian army pursuing them, they say to Moses: 'מַה־ זֹּאת עָשִׂיתָ לָּנוּ' ('What have you done to us?') and explicitly state they would have been better off remaining enslaved in Egypt rather than dying in the wilderness. They do not blame Yahweh; instead, they cry out to him for deliverance (וַיִּצְעֲקוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־ יְהוָֽה). This represents blame directed at their leader for the perilous situation, though not at the divine.
